These three must be in sync at all times; a discovered desync (e.g. a span-referenced code with no live strong row) is a FATAL ERROR, fixed on discovery, not merely logged. strong is the main operative: extended meaning is pulled from language-specific repositories (Hebrew+Greek: strong_meaning_tree/strong_meaning_parsed; Greek-only: strong_lexicon/strong_lsj_parsed/strong_mounce_parsed) and these must be absolutely in sync by language. Missing extended meaning is an ACCEPTED, non-fatal anomaly ONLY when explained by classification (T2/T3-T15/backfill -- see method rule spine-extended-meaning-accepted-anomaly), pulled on demand as analysis needs it, not proactively for every strong. Parse (strong_meaning_parsed/strong_lsj_parsed/strong_mounce_parsed) makes extended meaning digestible: every strong with extended meaning pulled MUST have a parse row; a break here is a FATAL ERROR, fixed on discovery. Once the spine is sound, verse-strong-parse is the whole route for meaning-in-context during analysis; if a term becomes significant during analysis and its parse is missing, pull it through on demand. Diagnosis: existing base-data incompleteness/errors trace to mismanagement of this spine, not unrelated bugs. Adjusted 2026-09-10 (escalations #1622-1624): discovery of a missing meaning/parse entry must TRIGGER its update at the point of discovery, not merely be logged for later.
